# Requirements — go-chi/chi v1.5.8

> Generated by [Quality Playbook](https://github.com/andrewstellman/quality-playbook) v1.6.0 — Andrew Stellman
> Date: 2026-07-19 · Project: go-chi/chi v1.5.8

Requirements document version: v2.0

---

## Overview

go-chi/chi is a lightweight HTTP router for Go built entirely on `net/http`. It registers
route patterns into a radix trie (`tree.go`), dispatches requests through a `Mux` (`mux.go`),
and carries per-request routing state — the matched pattern, the URL parameters, and the
mount-relative path still to be routed — in a `*chi.Context` stored on the request context
(`context.go`). Around that core sits a middleware library (`middleware/`) providing
compression, content negotiation, real-IP extraction, path rewriting, and related
request-shaping behavior.

Two audiences use chi and both are served by this specification. Application authors compose
routers: they call `Route()` and `Mount()` to build a tree of sub-routers, and they expect a
handler registered on a child to behave identically whether that child is mounted at `/` or at
`/api/v2`. Middleware authors and instrumentation consumers read chi's routing state: they call
`RoutePattern()`, `URLParam()`, `Walk()`, and `Mux.Find` and expect the values they get back to
describe the request chi is actually routing.

The design decision that shapes almost everything in this document is chi's split between the
raw `r.URL.Path` and its own canonical routing path, `rctx.RoutePath`. Under `Mount()`, the
dispatch closure rewrites `rctx.RoutePath` to the mount-relative remainder (`mux.go:309-322`,
`mux.go:383`) while `r.URL.Path` keeps carrying the full outer URL. The router walk reads
`rctx.RoutePath` first (`mux.go:441-456`). Any code that reads or writes the other
representation silently does the right thing on an unmounted router and the wrong thing the
moment a sub-router is introduced — a divergence that unit tests written against a flat router
never surface. A second recurring shape is the hand-maintained closed set: the HTTP-method
tables in `tree.go` and the compressible content-type whitelist in `middleware/compress.go`
must each stay in lock-step with every consumer, and drift between them is silent.

Requirements are derived from `quality/EXPLORATION.md` and cite specific files, functions, and
line numbers. Traceability is one-way REQ → UC; the reverse index is derived at render time in
the traceability appendix.

There is no `reference_docs/cite/` subdirectory in this tree, so there are **zero citable
formal-spec sources** — every requirement that cites an RFC cites an *external* standard
(RFC 7231, 7230, 7239, 2046), not a file in this repository. Such requirements are
"code inconsistency" candidates relative to chi's own docs, but "spec violations" relative
to the cited external standard, per the divergence-framing rules.

**Section ordering.** Functional sections run user-facing → infrastructure: the composition API
application authors call directly, then the wire-visible negotiation behavior their clients
observe, then the routing-table internals neither audience touches but both depend on.

**Coverage and known gaps.** This derivation covered chi's routing core (`mux.go`, `tree.go`,
`context.go`) and the middleware packages that manipulate the routing path or parse
RFC-defined request headers (`supress_notfound.go`, `page_route.go`, `path_rewrite.go`,
`strip.go`, `get_head.go`, `url_format.go`, `compress.go`, `content_charset.go`, `realip.go`).
It did **not** turn the remaining middleware into requirements: the logging, request-ID,
recoverer, throttling, timeout, and profiler middleware were skimmed for path- and
header-manipulation behavior and set aside once none was found — they carry their own
contracts that this pass makes no claim about. Concurrency contracts are also out of scope
here: chi's trie is documented as write-once-then-read, and this derivation did not attempt to
establish what happens when routes are registered concurrently with serving. No requirements
were derived for the `docgen` or example trees. Eight requirements for a router of this size is
a deliberately narrow, evidence-led set, not a full behavioral specification of chi.

## Actors and roles

**Application author.** Composes routers with `Route()` and `Mount()`, registers handlers, and
attaches middleware. Their central expectation is mount-transparency: a sub-router behaves the
same wherever it is mounted. REQ-001 through REQ-003 exist for this actor.

**Middleware author.** Writes code that runs inside chi's chain and inspects or rewrites the
request before the router walk. This actor must know which path representation is canonical,
because reading the wrong one is invisible until a sub-router appears. REQ-001 is written for
this actor directly.

**HTTP client and intervening proxy.** Sends `Accept-Encoding`, `Content-Type`, and
`X-Forwarded-For` in RFC-defined grammars and expects chi's middleware to honor them —
including the negative forms such as `q=0` that mean "do not do this." REQ-004 through REQ-006
serve this actor.

**Instrumentation and tooling consumer.** Reads `RoutePattern()`, `URLParam()`, `Walk()`, and
`Mux.Find` to label metrics, generate documentation, or enumerate routes. This actor never
issues requests; it reads chi's own reported state and needs that state to be faithful.
REQ-002, REQ-003, and REQ-008 serve this actor.

**chi maintainer.** Extends the closed sets — registering a new HTTP method, adding a
compressible content type — and needs those edits to propagate to every consumer. REQ-007 and
REQ-005 are the invariants that keep such edits safe.

## Composition and Mount-Context Awareness

chi's defining feature is sub-router composition via `Mount`/`Route`. The contract theme of
this section is **mount-transparency**: every path chi reports, matches against, or rewrites
must be expressed in the canonical mount-relative representation (`rctx.RoutePath`), so that
identical registrations behave identically whether or not a sub-router sits above them. Under
`Mount()`, chi maintains that canonical path (set in `mux.go:309-322` and `mux.go:383`)
diverging from the raw `r.URL.Path`, which always carries the full outer URL. Middleware and
lookup paths that read the wrong representation silently misbehave once a sub-router is
mounted. This section is first because `Mount` is the API application authors reach for on day
one.

### REQ-001: Canonical mount-relative path as the basis for path-manipulation middleware

Path-manipulation middleware must operate on chi's canonical mounted path (`rctx.RoutePath`),
not raw `r.URL.Path`, so behavior is correct under `Mount()`.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `SupressNotFound` (`middleware/supress_notfound.go:18-19`) must match against `rctx.RoutePath`, not `r.URL.Path`, when a sub-router is mounted, so a request to `/api/ping` under `root.Mount("/api", child)` consults the child trie key `/ping`.
  - `PageRoute` (`middleware/page_route.go:13`) must compare its configured path against `rctx.RoutePath` (the mount-relative path), not `r.URL.Path`, so `PageRoute("/status", h)` inside a `child` mounted at `/admin` fires for `/admin/status`.
  - `PathRewrite` (`middleware/path_rewrite.go:11-12`) must update the canonical routing path (`rctx.RoutePath`) it intends chi to route on, not only `r.URL.Path`, so the subsequent chi walk (which reads `rctx.RoutePath` first at `mux.go:441-456`) observes the rewrite.
  - Contrast (already correct): `StripSlashes` (`middleware/strip.go:17-29`), `GetHead` (`middleware/get_head.go:13-21`), `URLFormat` (`middleware/url_format.go:54-67`) read/write `rctx.RoutePath`.
- References: middleware/supress_notfound.go, middleware/page_route.go, middleware/path_rewrite.go
- Use cases: UC-1.a, UC-1.b, UC-1.c

### REQ-002: Context-effect parity between `Mux.Find`/`Mux.Match` and live routing on mounted routes

`Mux.Find`/`Mux.Match` must mirror live routing's observable context effects (including the
mount wildcard-URLParam reset) when traversing mounted routes.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - On a top-level (non-mounted) route, `Find` (`mux.go:368-393`) returns the matched pattern and leaves context state equivalent to a live walk through `routeHTTP` (`mux.go:460-484`).
  - On a mounted route, the live dispatch closure shifts `rctx.RoutePath = mx.nextRoutePath(rctx)` AND zeroes the connecting `*` URLParam (`mux.go:309-322`). `Find` must perform both effects: the same `RoutePath` shift it already performs (`mux.go:383`) and the wildcard-URLParam reset, so that a `Find` against a mounted route leaves no stale `*` URLParam behind. The two paths must agree on observable context effects, or `Find` must be documented as not mirroring URLParam side-effects.
- References: mux.go (mux.go:383 vs mux.go:309-322)
- Use cases: UC-4.a, UC-4.b

### REQ-003: Faithful `RoutePattern()` reconstruction for patterns holding a literal wildcard segment

`RoutePattern()` reconstruction must not corrupt patterns that contain a literal interior
wildcard segment.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `Context.RoutePattern()` (`context.go:123-134`) joins `RoutePatterns` and calls `replaceWildcards`, which loops `strings.ReplaceAll(p, "/*/", "/")` until no `/*/` remains (`context.go:136-144`). A route legitimately containing an interior `*` segment must not have that segment textually erased; the reported pattern must faithfully represent the registered pattern.
  - `walk()` performs the same collapse on full routes (`tree.go:862`) and must preserve a literal interior `*` segment identically.
  - The trailing-`//`/`/` `TrimSuffix` order (`context.go:129-132`) must not strip a legitimate trailing component.
- References: context.go, tree.go
- Use cases: UC-5.a, UC-5.b

## Content Negotiation and Compression Correctness

This section's contract theme is **wire-level honesty in negotiated responses**: what chi
accepts from a client's headers, what it decides is eligible for compression, and what it then
claims on the response must all agree with each other and with the RFC grammars the headers are
written in. The three requirements form one causal chain — a parse that over-accepts
(REQ-004) selects an encoder, an eligibility set that is not authoritative (REQ-005) admits the
wrong body, and the response writer then declares an encoding it did not apply (REQ-006). They
are grouped because fixing any one in isolation leaves the observable defect reachable through
the others. It follows composition because these behaviors are observed by clients rather than
configured by the application author.

### REQ-004: Grammar-faithful parsing of RFC-defined request headers

RFC-defined request-header parsing must follow the grammar (tokenize on the list separator,
honor `q=0`, trim whitespace, parse parameters, match exact coding names), not substring/`Cut`
shortcuts.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - **Accept-Encoding (`middleware/compress.go:212-246`):** `matchAcceptEncoding` must accept a coding iff it appears as an exact comma-list token (after whitespace trim) with a non-zero q-value. `Accept-Encoding: gzip;q=0` (explicit rejection per RFC 7231 §5.3.4) must NOT select gzip; a bogus token like `xgzip` or `notgzip` (which `strings.Contains` falsely matches) must NOT select gzip. Comma elements must be `TrimSpace`d.
  - **Content-Type charset (`middleware/content_charset.go:29-34`):** `contentEncoding` must match a quoted charset such as `charset="utf-8"` and must not be fooled by a `charset` substring appearing inside another parameter value.
  - **X-Forwarded-For (`middleware/realip.go:42-56`):** `realIP` must `TrimSpace` the leftmost comma segment before `net.ParseIP`, so a producer that pads the first element with a leading space (`" 203.0.113.1"`) does not silently leave `RemoteAddr` unchanged. Parse failures must not be masked beyond what RFC 7239 / the doc comment (`middleware/realip.go:24-30`) intend.
- References: middleware/compress.go, middleware/content_charset.go, middleware/realip.go
- Use cases: UC-2

### REQ-005: Compressible content-type whitelist as the single source of compression eligibility

The compressible content-type whitelist must gate compression consistently with its membership
check, and its closed set must be the single source of truth for eligibility.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `defaultCompressibleContentTypes` (`middleware/compress.go:16-27`) is the closed set; `isCompressible` (`middleware/compress.go:274-288`) must decide eligibility by exact membership after stripping `;`-parameters, plus the wildcard set (`allowedWildcards`) only when configured.
  - A content type NOT in the set (and not matched by a configured wildcard) must not be compressed; a content type in the set must be eligible. The set membership must not be bypassed or duplicated elsewhere.
- References: middleware/compress.go
- Use cases: UC-6

### REQ-006: `Content-Encoding` declared only for bodies the writer actually compresses

`compressResponseWriter` must not declare `Content-Encoding` for a body it does not actually
compress.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `WriteHeader` (`middleware/compress.go:298-316`) sets `Content-Encoding: <cw.encoding>` and deletes `Content-Length` only when the content is compressible and an encoder was selected; `writer()` (`middleware/compress.go:326-331`) must return the encoding writer iff `cw.compressible`. The declared `Content-Encoding` must match the bytes actually written.
  - Because `cw.encoding` is populated by `selectEncoder` purely from the (substring-matched) Accept-Encoding header (REQ-004), a false-accept (`xgzip`) must not result in `Content-Encoding: gzip` over uncompressed bytes — fixing REQ-004 closes this surface.
- References: middleware/compress.go
- Use cases: UC-7

## Routing Table and Parameter Integrity

The contract theme here is **internal representations that must stay in lock-step**. chi keeps
hand-maintained closed sets and parallel key/value slices that no single function owns end to
end: the HTTP-method tables are written by one function and read by three unrelated consumers,
and the parameter arrays are pushed and unwound at two structurally similar backtracking sites.
Drift in either is silent — nothing panics, and the router keeps answering; it simply answers
with the wrong method set or the wrong parameter value. These are infrastructure invariants
neither the application author nor the client can observe directly, which is why they are last
and why they need mechanical verification rather than example-driven tests.

### REQ-007: HTTP-method closed-set consistency across `methodMap`, `reverseMethodMap`, and `mALL`

The HTTP-method closed set must stay consistent across all three structures (`methodMap`,
`reverseMethodMap`, `mALL`) and every consumer.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `methodMap` (`tree.go:35-45`), `reverseMethodMap` (`tree.go:47-57`), and `mALL` (`tree.go:32-33`) must enumerate exactly the same method set. Every key in `methodMap` must have a matching value in `reverseMethodMap` (and vice versa), and `mALL` must equal the bitwise OR of every `methodMap` bit.
  - `RegisterMethod` (`tree.go:61-77`) must update all three structures together (it does: `methodMap[method]=mt`, `reverseMethodMap[mt]=method`, `mALL |= mt`).
  - Consumers must observe a consistent set: `routeHTTP` 405s when `RouteMethod` is absent from `methodMap` (`mux.go:462-466`); `methodNotAllowedHandler` builds `Allow` from `reverseMethodMap` (`mux.go:518-526`); the wildcard registration fans across `methodMap` entries (`tree.go:355-365`).
- References: tree.go, mux.go
- Use cases: UC-3

### REQ-008: Keys/Values length consistency across both `findRoute` backtracking unwind sites

`findRoute` param backtracking must keep `routeParams.Keys` and `routeParams.Values`
length-consistent across both unwind sites, so `URLParam` index reads never misalign.

- Conditions of satisfaction:
  - `findRoute` (`tree.go:457-490`, `tree.go:534-539`) pushes a candidate param value and unwinds on failure via two structurally similar cleanup sites; both must keep Keys/Values length-consistent.
  - `FindRoute` appends `paramKeys` to `URLParams` assuming exact Keys↔Values correspondence (`tree.go:386-394`); `Context.URLParam` reads by reverse-index match (`context.go:100-107`). No backtracking path through mixed param/regexp/catch-all siblings may leave a Keys/Values length skew.
- References: tree.go, context.go
- Use cases: UC-8

## Cross-cutting concerns

**One canonical path representation.** The single invariant that spans every section of this
document is that `rctx.RoutePath` — not `r.URL.Path` — is chi's authoritative statement of what
is still to be routed. REQ-001 states it for middleware, REQ-002 states it for the lookup APIs,
and REQ-003 states it for the pattern chi reports back. A change to how mount-relative paths are
computed in `mux.go` touches all three at once, and a fix applied to only one of them leaves the
inconsistency reachable through the others.

**Closed sets are single-source-of-truth or they are nothing.** REQ-005 and REQ-007 are the same
contract over different data: a hand-maintained set whose membership decides behavior must be
consulted exactly once, by exact membership, with every parallel structure updated in the same
edit. Both closed sets are extensible at runtime or by configuration (`RegisterMethod`,
`allowedWildcards`), so the invariant must hold after extension, not merely at initialization.

**Silent-divergence failure philosophy.** None of these requirements protect against a crash.
Every violation in this document produces a wrong answer that the process reports as success —
a spurious 404, an unmatched route, a corrupted pattern string, a `Content-Encoding` header over
plaintext, a parameter read from the wrong index. That shapes verification: the conditions of
satisfaction are written to be checked by differential and mechanical means (mounted versus
unmounted, table versus consumer, declared versus written), because no exception will surface
them.

**External specs, no internal spec.** REQ-004 and REQ-006 measure chi against RFC 7231, 7230,
7239, and 2046, none of which are vendored into this repository. Divergences found against them
are spec violations with respect to the external standard and code inconsistencies with respect
to chi's own documentation — a distinction that matters when reporting upstream, and one that
applies to no other requirement here.

**Backward compatibility.** chi's observable outputs — the `Allow` header contents, the string
returned by `RoutePattern()`, whether a response carries `Content-Encoding` — are depended on by
instrumentation and by proxies outside this repository. Every requirement in this document
constrains a value that has already shipped, so satisfying it means correcting behavior for
inputs that are currently mishandled, not changing behavior for inputs that already work.

## Use cases

Use cases describe end-to-end user-observable outcomes. They render `formal_doc_refs` (none
here — no citable formal docs) but do NOT list `requirements[]`; traceability is one-way
REQ → UC, and the reverse index is derived in the traceability appendix below.

### UC-1.a: `SupressNotFound` under a mounted sub-router
- Actors: chi `Mux`, an operator mounting a sub-router, an HTTP client
- Preconditions: `root.Mount("/api", child)`; `child` uses `SupressNotFound`
- Flow: request `/api/ping`; middleware must `Match` against the canonical `rctx.RoutePath` (`/ping`), not `r.URL.Path` (`/api/ping`), using a throwaway context
- Postconditions: a defined `/ping` route is found; no spurious 404; live `rctx` unmutated
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-1.b: `PageRoute` under a mounted sub-router
- Actors: chi `Mux`, operator, client
- Preconditions: `root.Mount("/admin", child)`; `child` uses `PageRoute("/status", h)`
- Flow: request `/admin/status`; the match must compare against `rctx.RoutePath` (`/status`)
- Postconditions: `PageRoute` fires for the mounted path
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-1.c: `PathRewrite` under a mounted sub-router
- Actors: chi `Mux`, operator, client
- Preconditions: `root.Mount("/svc", child)`; `child` uses `PathRewrite(old,new)`
- Flow: rewrite must update the canonical routing path so chi's subsequent walk (which reads `rctx.RoutePath`) observes the rewrite
- Postconditions: chi routes the rewritten path, not the original
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-2: RFC-correct request-header parsing (umbrella)
- Actors: compression/content-negotiation/real-IP middleware, HTTP client behind a proxy
- Preconditions: client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip;q=0` / `Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"` / padded or ported `X-Forwarded-For`
- Flow: each parser tokenizes per its RFC (q-value honored, quoted params handled, whitespace trimmed) before deciding
- Postconditions: `q=0` suppresses compression; quoted charset matched; valid XFF entries accepted
- formal_doc_refs: (none — external RFC 7231/7230/7239/2046)

### UC-3: HTTP-method closed-set consistency (umbrella)
- Actors: chi `Mux`, application calling `RegisterMethod`
- Preconditions: a custom method is registered, or a request uses an unsupported method
- Flow: `methodMap`, `reverseMethodMap`, and `mALL` are updated together; `routeHTTP` and the 405 `Allow` builder read a consistent set
- Postconditions: `Allow` header lists exactly the registered methods; wildcard registration covers the new method
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-4.a: `Find` mirrors live routing on a top-level route
- Actors: code calling `Mux.Find`
- Preconditions: a registered non-mounted route
- Flow: `Find` returns the pattern with the same context effects as a live walk
- Postconditions: pattern returned; context state consistent
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-4.b: `Find` mirrors live routing on a mounted route
- Actors: code calling `Mux.Find` against a mounted sub-router
- Preconditions: `root.Mount("/api", child)`
- Flow: `Find` shifts `RoutePath` AND performs the wildcard-URLParam reset the live closure does
- Postconditions: returned pattern and resulting context match the live path exactly
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-5.a: `RoutePattern()` for a route with a trailing wildcard
- Actors: instrumentation middleware reading `RoutePattern()`
- Preconditions: route `/files/*`
- Flow: `replaceWildcards` collapses only synthesized mount wildcards
- Postconditions: reported pattern preserves a legitimate trailing `*`
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-5.b: `walk()` full-route reconstruction with an interior literal `*`
- Actors: `Walk` consumers (docgen, route listing)
- Preconditions: a route whose pattern legitimately contains an interior `*` segment
- Flow: the `/*/`→`/` collapse must not erase a literal interior segment
- Postconditions: the walked full route is faithful to the registered pattern
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-6: Compressible content-type whitelist completeness
- Actors: chi `Compress` middleware, an HTTP client requesting compression
- Preconditions: a response with a content type in `defaultCompressibleContentTypes` vs one not in it
- Flow: `isCompressible` decides eligibility by exact membership (plus configured wildcards)
- Postconditions: only whitelisted (or wildcard-configured) types are compressed
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-7: Compression writer does not over-declare `Content-Encoding`
- Actors: chi `Compress` middleware, an HTTP client
- Preconditions: a request whose Accept-Encoding falsely selects an encoder (REQ-004 surface)
- Flow: `WriteHeader`/`writer()` couple so the declared `Content-Encoding` matches the bytes written
- Postconditions: no `Content-Encoding` header on a body that was not actually compressed
- formal_doc_refs: (none)

### UC-8: Param backtracking keeps Keys/Values aligned
- Actors: chi router walking a deep tree with mixed param/regexp/catch-all siblings
- Preconditions: a registration set that forces backtracking across sibling node types
- Flow: `findRoute` unwinds candidate values without skewing Keys vs Values length
- Postconditions: `URLParam` returns the correct value by index; no param misalignment
- formal_doc_refs: (none)
